biologicalRelevance: Crucial absolute component of all living structures, cellular water, and matrices.
nuclearProperties: Highly stable nuclear configuration with 0 neutrons bound tightly to 1 protons by the strong nuclear force. Resists nuclear fission.

physicalProperties.magneticProperties: Ferromagnetic (exhibits powerful spontaneous permanent magnetic ordering)

chemicalProperties.reactivityProfile: Active post-transition metal. Corrodes progressively in moist oxygen atmospheres (rusts) and dissolves quickly in mineral acids.

cosmicProperties.stellarOrigin: Core silicon burning in massive pre-supernova stars
cosmicProperties.nucleosynthesisProcess: Equilibrium alpha-process (silicon burning) and nickel-56 decay
cosmicProperties.cosmicAbundance: 0.11% by mass of the atomic universe
cosmicProperties.earthAbundance: 5.63% of Crust, comprises ~90% of Earth's core with Nickel
cosmicProperties.planetaryPresence: Sinks to form the massive, liquid electromagnetic cores of active rocky worlds
cosmicProperties.stellarPresence: The definitive final core endpoint of standard non-fusing main-sequence stars

biologicalProperties.biologicalImportance: Essential transition metal trace element vital for blood oxygen transport and enzymatic cells.
biologicalProperties.humanBodyPresence: 0.006% of total body mass (representing about 4.2 grams in average adult cells)
biologicalProperties.toxicity: Highly toxic in unbound free states; causes oxidative free radical damage.
biologicalProperties.nutritionalRelevance: Highly vital nutritional mineral sourced from meat, eggs, and spinach.
biologicalProperties.biologicalFunction: Acts as the central coordination anchor inside hemoglobin and myoglobin proteins to capture oxygen.

historicalProperties.namingOrigin: From Anglo-Saxon 'iren'. Symbol 'Fe' is derived from Latin 'ferrum' (strength/firm).
historicalProperties.historicalSignificance: Drove humanity out of the Bronze Age into the Iron Age, shaping structural mechanics, wars, and architectures.
majorScientificMilestones: Pre-3000 BC: Extraction of meteor iron beads for pharaonic elite daggers
1200 BC: Standardized charcoal blast furnace smelting opens the Iron Age
1856: Bessemer process invented, making mass steel production cheap
1912: Invention of stainless chromium-iron steel alloys resisting corrosion

dangerousReactions: Finely powdered pyrophoric iron dust ignites spontaneously in dry air

synthesisPossibilities: Industrial Bessemer steel smelting and carbon-carbon alloying

atomicArchitecture.orbitalBreakdown: Valence electron shell configurations represented by [Rn] 5f¹⁴ 6d2 7s2. Outer electrons fill orbitals orderly based on Hund's Rule and Pauli Exclusion principles.
atomicArchitecture.nuclearProperties: Highly unstable, radioactive nucleus. Decay modes include spontaneous alpha/beta emissions or spontaneous fission. Half-life is extremely brief.

physicalProperties.thermalConductivity: Very High (~50-300 W/(m·K)) due to d-shell free electron coupling
physicalProperties.electricalConductivity: Exceptional (~1.0 x 10^7 to 4.5 x 10^7 S/m) electron travel
physicalProperties.magneticProperties: Paramagnetic (weakly attracted by external magnetic fields due to presence of unpaired orbital spins)

chemicalProperties.reactivityProfile: Moderate reactivity. Forms oxides slowly, reacting with hot mineral acids and active molecular halogens.
chemicalProperties.bondingCharacteristics: Prefers covalent d-orbital electron sharing or directional coordination metallic lattices.

cosmicProperties.stellarOrigin: Supernova r-process stellar shockwaves and binary neutron star collisions
